license_note: Dimensional values are facts fixed by published standards (ISO 261/262 pitches, ISO 724 basic profile, ISO 273 clearance holes, ISO 4762 socket head cap screws, ISO 10642 countersunk and ISO 7380-1 button head socket screws, ISO 4032 style 1 hex nuts, ISO 4035 thin nuts, DIN 985 / ISO 7040 nylon-insert nuts, ISO 7089 plain washers, ISO 898-1 property classes, ISO 3506-1 stainless classes, ASME B94.11M drill sizes, DIN 974-1 counterbores). The standards documents are copyright ISO/DIN/ASME; the numbers are not. PROVENANCE: the values were compiled from memory of those standards (standards bodies unreachable from this environment) and then independently re-derived from memory by three reviewers plus a partial check of the M2-M8 SHCS head and tap-drill columns against nophead/NopSCADlib vitamins/screws.scad. The values are standard-fixed; the compilation is from memory; therefore no row is labelled 'certain' - only fields that are fixed by formula (pitch, d3, D1, sharp across-corners, inch-to-mm conversions, fractional drills) carry 'certain' in field_confidence. Tap drills, engagement-length, counterbore-depth and torque rules are trade practice / design rules, not standard values, and say so in their column descriptions.

columns.key: unique row id (thread designation, coarse pitch)
columns.minor_d_mm: mm, basic minor diameter of the EXTERNAL thread d3 = d - 1.22687p, ISO 724 (3 dp). Use for bolt shank / thread-root modelling only
columns.minor_D1_mm: mm, basic minor diameter of the INTERNAL thread D1 = d - 1.08253p, ISO 724 (3 dp). This is what a tapped hole presents; model tapped holes at D1, never at d3
columns.tap_drill_mm: mm, conventional tap drill, d - p rule (~77% thread on the Machinery's Handbook definition) rounded to a stock drill. TRADE PRACTICE, not an ISO value. For cut taps in aluminium, brass, mild/free-machining steel. NOT for form/roll taps and NOT for wire-thread inserts (see sti_insert_drill_mm)
columns.tap_drill_pct_thread: %, thread engagement of tap_drill_mm, = 100 (d - drill) / (1.299 p) (Machinery's Handbook)
columns.tap_drill_stainless_mm: mm, larger tap drill d - 0.85p rounded to 0.1 mm (~62-68% thread) for stainless, titanium and thin sections to reduce tap breakage. TRADE PRACTICE. Strength above ~65% engagement is governed by engagement LENGTH, not percentage (see min_engagement_6061T6_8_8_mm)
columns.tap_drill_stainless_pct_thread: %, thread engagement of tap_drill_stainless_mm, same formula
columns.sti_insert_drill_mm: mm, tap drill for a wire-thread (STI / HELICOIL / Recoil type) insert of the SAME nominal size. RECALL - insert makers' charts differ by ~0.1 mm; verify against the insert maker's chart before drilling. null = not supplied
columns.us_tap_drill: nearest US number / letter / fractional drill to tap_drill_mm, ASME B94.11M; engagement % shifts slightly (see the _mm value)
columns.us_tap_drill_in: inch, decimal size of that US drill exactly as ASME B94.11M lists it
columns.clearance_fine_mm: mm, ISO 273 fine series clearance hole (H12): precisely located, jig-drilled patterns only
columns.clearance_medium_mm: mm, ISO 273 medium series clearance hole (H13): the default for machined flight parts
columns.clearance_coarse_mm: mm, ISO 273 coarse series clearance hole (H14): sheet / welded structures
columns.us_clearance_drill: nearest US number / letter / fractional drill to clearance_medium_mm (falls between fine and coarse), ASME B94.11M
columns.us_clearance_drill_in: inch, decimal size of that US drill exactly as ASME B94.11M lists it
columns.shcs_head_d_mm: mm, ISO 4762 socket head cap screw head diameter dk MAX for a PLAIN (non-knurled) head. WARNING: common vendor stock is knurled and is larger - size counterbores from shcs_head_d_knurled_mm or cbore_d_mm, never from this column
columns.shcs_head_d_knurled_mm: mm, ISO 4762 dk max for a KNURLED head (the larger of the two dk maxima in the standard). Use this for counterbore / pocket clearance
columns.shcs_head_h_mm: mm, ISO 4762 head height k max (= d nominal)
columns.shcs_hex_key_mm: mm, ISO 4762 hexagon socket s nominal (hex key across flats)
columns.shcs_thread_len_b_mm: mm, ISO 4762 reference thread length b = 2d + 12 for screws long enough to have a plain shank; shorter screws are supplied fully threaded. Unthreaded shank ds max = d nominal, so it always passes the clearance hole. Check thread run-out against stacked parts
columns.cbore_d_mm: mm, counterbore diameter for an ISO 4762 SHCS without washer, DIN 974-1 style values. RECALL. Any value >= shcs_head_d_knurled_mm + 0.4 works; these are the standard counterbore-tool sizes
columns.cbore_depth_flush_mm: mm, minimum counterbore depth for a flush head = shcs_head_h_mm (k max) + 0.5. DESIGN RULE, not a standard value. Add washer_t_mm if a washer sits under the head
columns.csk_head_d_mm: mm, ISO 10642 90-degree countersunk socket screw head diameter dk THEORETICAL SHARP max; countersink to this diameter at 90 deg for a flush head. RECALL. null = size not in ISO 10642 (M2, M2.5)
columns.csk_head_h_mm: mm, ISO 10642 head height k max (theoretical). RECALL
columns.csk_hex_key_mm: mm, ISO 10642 hexagon socket s. RECALL
columns.button_head_d_mm: mm, ISO 7380-1 button head socket screw dk max. RECALL. null = size not in ISO 7380-1 (M2, M2.5, M14, M20)
columns.button_head_h_mm: mm, ISO 7380-1 head height k max. RECALL
columns.button_hex_key_mm: mm, ISO 7380-1 hexagon socket s. RECALL
columns.nut_af_mm: mm, ISO 4032 style 1 hex nut width across flats s max (= nominal). A hex POCKET must also clear the corners: see nut_ac_min_mm / nut_ac_sharp_mm
columns.nut_ac_min_mm: mm, ISO 4032 width across corners e MIN (the smallest corner span a conforming nut presents, corners chamfered)
columns.nut_ac_sharp_mm: mm, theoretical sharp-corner span = nut_af_mm / cos 30 deg (3 dp). A true-hex pocket cut to AF + clearance clears this automatically; a pocket milled with a round cutter needs corner relief to at least this diameter
columns.din934_nut_af_mm: mm, DIN 934 across flats where it differs from ISO 4032 (M10 17, M12 19, M14 22); null = same as ISO. Many vendors still ship DIN-sized nuts - check stock before cutting a pocket
columns.nut_h_mm: mm, ISO 4032 style 1 hex nut height m MAX. Size pocket depth to this
columns.nut_h_min_mm: mm, ISO 4032 style 1 hex nut height m MIN. Do not size anything that must not bottom out from m max alone
columns.locknut_h_mm: mm, nylon-insert prevailing-torque hex nut height max, DIN 985 / ISO 7040 family. RECALL. ISO 10511 thin type is lower and DIN 985 M10 is 17 AF (ISO 16). A pocket cut to nut_h_mm will NOT accept a nyloc. null = not supplied
columns.jam_nut_h_mm: mm, ISO 4035 (DIN 439) thin / jam hex nut height m max. RECALL
columns.washer_id_mm: mm, ISO 7089 plain washer normal series d1 (nominal = min); equals the ISO 273 fine clearance hole
columns.washer_od_mm: mm, ISO 7089 plain washer normal series d2 (nominal = max); use as spot-face diameter minimum
columns.washer_t_mm: mm, ISO 7089 plain washer normal series thickness h nominal
columns.tensile_stress_area_mm2: mm^2, ISO 898-1 nominal tensile stress area As,nom = (pi/4)((d2+d3)/2)^2, printed to 3 sf as the standard does
columns.proof_load_8_8_N: N, As,nom x proof stress Sp, class 8.8 (580 MPa for d <= 16, 600 MPa for d > 16), 3 sf. COMPUTED from As; ISO 898-1 Table 7 prints values that may differ by rounding (< 1%)
columns.proof_load_10_9_N: N, As,nom x 830 MPa, 3 sf, computed
columns.proof_load_12_9_N: N, As,nom x 970 MPa, 3 sf, computed
columns.proof_load_A2_70_N: N, As,nom x 450 MPa (ISO 3506-1 Rp0.2 for class 70), 3 sf, computed
columns.torque_guide_8_8_dry_Nm: N*m, tightening-torque GUIDE for class 8.8, plain/dry, T = K F d with K = 0.20 and F = 0.7 x proof load, 3 sf. DESIGN RULE. Lubricated / plated: K ~ 0.14-0.16 (multiply by 0.7-0.8). Other classes: scale by proof-stress ratio (10.9 x1.43, 12.9 x1.67, A2-70 x0.78). Agrees with the commonly published VDI 2230 mu=0.14 / 90% yield tables within ~5%
columns.min_engagement_6061T6_8_8_mm: mm, minimum thread engagement length for a class 8.8 bolt in a tapped 6061-T6 aluminium part so that the internal thread does not strip before the bolt breaks: Le = As x 800 MPa / (0.5 pi d tau), tau = 0.6 x 310 MPa, rounded UP to 0.5 mm (works out to 1.5-1.7d). DESIGN RULE with a simplified shear area (~0.5 pi d Le). Scale by bolt UTS ratio: 10.9 x1.3 (~2.0-2.2d), 12.9 x1.5 (~2.3-2.6d), A2-70 x0.875 (~1.3-1.5d). Other parent materials: multiply by 186 / (0.6 x parent UTS in MPa), e.g. 7075-T6 x0.55, mild steel x0.75, PEEK/polymers x3 or more. Add 1-2 pitches for chamfer and incomplete threads
columns.confidence: certain | likely | recall - the ROW label covers the fields listed in core_fields; every field whose confidence differs from the row label, and every non-core field, has its own entry in field_confidence
columns.field_confidence: object, {field: certain|likely|recall} for fields whose confidence differs from the row label and for all supplementary (non-core) fields
columns.disputed: object (only where present), {field: [alternative values with who gave them]} - reviewers disagreed; the tabulated value is the reconciler's pick and the field is marked recall
columns.source: row-level pointer; the authoritative field -> standard mapping is field_sources

field_sources.tap_drill_mm: trade practice (d - p rounded to stock drill), e.g. DIN 336 / vendor tap-drill charts; % formula Machinery's Handbook
field_sources.us_tap_drill: ASME B94.11M-1993 drill size table, nearest to tap_drill_mm
field_sources.us_clearance_drill: ASME B94.11M-1993 drill size table, nearest to clearance_medium_mm
field_sources.tensile_stress_area_mm2: ISO 898-1:2013 Table A.1 / Annex A, As,nom
field_sources.proof_load_8_8_N: computed from ISO 898-1:2013 Table 3 Sp and As,nom
field_sources.proof_load_10_9_N: computed from ISO 898-1:2013 Table 3 Sp and As,nom
field_sources.proof_load_12_9_N: computed from ISO 898-1:2013 Table 3 Sp and As,nom
field_sources.proof_load_A2_70_N: computed from ISO 3506-1:2020 Table 4 Rp0.2 and As,nom
field_sources.torque_guide_8_8_dry_Nm: design rule T = K F d (Machinery's Handbook / VDI 2230 order of magnitude)
field_sources.min_engagement_6061T6_8_8_mm: design rule, internal-thread strip check (Machinery's Handbook / FED-STD-H28 simplified shear area)

8.8.note: d <= 16 mm. For d > 16 mm (M20 here) ISO 898-1 gives proof 600, yield 660, UTS 830; proof_load_8_8_N already uses 600 for M20

12.9.note: hydrogen-embrittlement sensitive; avoid electroplated (zinc) 12.9 on flight parts - use black-oxide or plain. In tapped aluminium a 12.9 bolt needs ~2.3d engagement or the aluminium thread strips first

A2-70.note: ISO 3506-1 austenitic stainless, cold-worked. Property classes 70 and 80 apply to thread sizes up to and INCLUDING M24; above M24 class 50 (proof 210, UTS 500) is the usual supply unless agreed. yield_MPa is Rp0.2 (the standard specifies a 0.2% proof stress, not a distinct yield). A2-80 is 600 / 800. STRENGTH TRAP: A2-70 proof (450) is only 78% of 8.8 (580), 54% of 10.9 (830) and 46% of 12.9 (970) - substituting stainless for a carbon-steel callout on a pressure-vessel end cap or retainer REQUIRES re-checking preload and clamp load. A2 screws gall against A2 nuts - use anti-seize or an A2/A4 mix
A2-70.source: ISO 3506-1:2020 Table 4 (size range: ISO 3506-1:2009 Table 3 footnote, recall)

size_range: <= M24 (fitness skeptic, ISO 3506-1:2020 Table 4; reconciler agrees)
<= M24 in the 2009 edition, the 2020 edition may extend class 70 further (spot-check skeptic, unverified)

A2-50.note: soft (annealed) class; usual supply above M24

grades.grades_confidence: likely for every class (standard-fixed numbers confirmed by three independent recalls; compiled from memory so not labelled certain)

thread_engagement_length.rule: Minimum engagement of a bolt in a tapped hole, as multiples of d: steel-in-steel 1.0d; class 8.8 in 6061-T6 aluminium 1.5-1.7d; 10.9 in 6061-T6 2.0-2.2d; 12.9 in 6061-T6 2.3-2.6d; A2-70 in 6061-T6 1.3-1.5d; any bolt in 7075-T6 ~0.55x the 6061 value; soft alloys / polymers 2.5-3d or more. These come from Le = F_ult,bolt / (0.5 pi d tau_parent) with tau = 0.6 UTS_parent (see min_engagement_6061T6_8_8_mm); add 1-2 pitches for chamfer / incomplete threads. This is the governing failure mode for a tapped aluminium pressure-vessel end cap or bulkhead - the aluminium thread strips long before an 8.8 bolt breaks if Le is short. Thread PERCENTAGE above ~65% adds almost nothing; engagement LENGTH is what matters in aluminium
thread_engagement_length.source: Machinery's Handbook (internal thread stripping), FED-STD-H28 simplified; 6061-T6 UTS 310 MPa min per ASTM B221

edge_distance.rule: Hole centre to part edge >= 1.5d for clearance holes and >= 2d for tapped holes in aluminium (>= 1.5d in steel); minimum wall around a tapped boss >= 1d (>= 0.5d absolute floor in steel). Thin centering rings and couplers frequently violate this - check before adding a hole pattern
edge_distance.source: common machine-design practice (Shigley / Machinery's Handbook), not a standard

preload_and_torque.rule: Target preload F = 0.65-0.75 x proof load (see proof_load_* columns). Torque T = K F d, K = 0.20 plain dry, 0.14-0.16 lubricated or zinc-plated, ~0.12 with anti-seize; ISO 16047 friction classes cover the same range. torque_guide_8_8_dry_Nm tabulates K = 0.2, F = 0.7 proof for 8.8. Torque scatter is +/-25% even with a calibrated wrench - do not rely on torque alone for a pressure boundary
preload_and_torque.source: Machinery's Handbook / VDI 2230 / ISO 16047, design rule

inserts_and_form_taps.rule: tap_drill_mm and tap_drill_stainless_mm are for CUT taps only. Wire-thread inserts (HELICOIL / Recoil, STI) need the larger sti_insert_drill_mm and an STI tap; solid inserts (Keensert / Time-Sert) need their own drill and tap; form (roll) taps need a drill near D1 + 0.1-0.2 mm (roughly d - 0.5p) - use the tap maker's chart. Inserts are the normal repair / upgrade for tapped aluminium flight parts and effectively move the strip check to the insert's outer thread
inserts_and_form_taps.source: insert and tap makers' charts; trade practice

notes: USAGE. (1) Coarse pitch only; fine-pitch threads (M8x1, M10x1.25, M12x1.25 ...) are NOT in this table and have different minor diameters, tap drills and stress areas. (2) Model tapped holes at minor_D1_mm (internal thread D1); use minor_d_mm (external d3) only for bolt roots. Both are now tabulated for every size. (3) Tap drills: tap_drill_mm is the d - p rule (~77% thread) rounded to a stock drill (M8: 6.75 -> 6.8; M12: 10.25 -> 10.2; NopSCADlib carries 6.75 for M8 - not an error, a rounding choice). tap_drill_stainless_mm is d - 0.85p (~62-68%). Engagement percentage above ~65% adds almost no strength in steel and NONE that matters in aluminium, where engagement LENGTH governs - see design_rules.thread_engagement_length and min_engagement_6061T6_8_8_mm. Never use these drills for form taps or wire-thread inserts (design_rules.inserts_and_form_taps; sti_insert_drill_mm). US number/letter/fraction equivalents are given for shops that stock only an inch drill index; the % thread shifts by a few points (e.g. M4 #30 gives ~81%, M2.5 #46 gives ~76%). (4) Clearance holes: ISO 273 medium series is the default for machined flight parts; fine for jig-drilled patterns; coarse for sheet / welded structures. Tolerance grades: fine H12, medium H13, coarse H14. (5) SHCS: shcs_head_d_mm is the PLAIN-head dk max; vendor stock is usually KNURLED and larger - shcs_head_d_knurled_mm is now a column for all 12 sizes and cbore_d_mm / cbore_depth_flush_mm give the counterbore. cbore_d_mm is recall (DIN 974-1 style); any diameter >= knurled dk + 0.4 works. Counterbore depth for a flush head = k + 0.5 (+ washer thickness if washered). Countersunk (ISO 10642) and button-head (ISO 7380-1) heads are tabulated as recall for the sizes those standards cover; countersink at 90 deg to csk_head_d_mm (theoretical sharp). (6) Nuts: ISO 4032 AF differs from DIN 934 at M10 (16 / 17), M12 (18 / 19), M14 (21 / 22) - din934_nut_af_mm flags these; vendors often still ship DIN sizes, check stock before cutting a pocket. A captured-nut hex pocket must clear the CORNERS: nut_ac_min_mm is the ISO 4032 e min, nut_ac_sharp_mm the theoretical sharp span (AF / cos 30). nut_h_mm is m max (size pocket depth to it); nut_h_min_mm is m min - the max-min spread is 0.25-0.3 mm at M2-M6, 0.36-0.43 mm at M8-M12 and 0.7-1.1 mm at M14-M20 (the compiled table's '0.4-0.5 mm for M6 and up' aside was wrong for M14-M20 and has been replaced by the column). Reviewers disagreed on m min for M6 (4.9 vs 4.7) and M8 (6.44 vs 6.14): those two cells are marked recall with the alternatives in 'disputed'. Flight hardware is normally LOCKED: a pocket cut to nut_h_mm will not take a nyloc - locknut_h_mm (DIN 985 / ISO 7040 family, recall, roughly = d) and jam_nut_h_mm (ISO 4035, recall) are supplied. (7) Washers: ISO 7089 normal series 200 HV (same as DIN 125A at every size in this table). ISO 7092 small and ISO 7093 large (fender) series differ. washer_od_mm is the minimum spot-face diameter for a nut / bolt-head seat. (8) Strength: tensile_stress_area_mm2 is ISO 898-1 As,nom. proof_load_* = As x Sp (computed, 3 sf; the standard's printed Table 7 values may differ by rounding). torque_guide_8_8_dry_Nm and min_engagement_6061T6_8_8_mm are DESIGN RULES derived from the tabulated numbers, not standard values - see design_rules for the formulas and how to scale to other classes and parent materials. The grades object is now a parseable top-level key; note the A2-70 strength trap recorded there. (9) Confidence scheme: the row label covers the fields in core_fields; field_confidence lists every supplementary field (all recall or design-rule 'likely') and every core field that differs. No row is 'certain' because the whole compilation is from memory; fields fixed by formula or exact conversion are 'certain' in field_confidence. Least trusted: nut_h_min_mm at M2-M8 (M6, M8 disputed), cbore_d_mm, locknut_h_mm, jam_nut_h_mm, csk_*, button_*, sti_insert_drill_mm - all recall. (10) Rows dropped: none (the fitness reviewer found no row too uncertain to cut from). Before cutting a pressure-vessel or structural part, cross-check the specific row against a vendor catalogue (Bossard, Wurth, McMaster-Carr ISO pages) - especially any recall-labelled field.
